news.originalContent:

The president and CEO of the American Psychological Association rejected the findings of a House report on Jew-hatred in the association, telling colleagues on Thursday that the APA has “held listening sessions” with Jewish psychologists.

“The APA’s actions not only create a harmful environment for Jewish members but also raise broader concerns about the profession,” a House Committee on Education and Workforce spokesperson told JNS.

“When an organization responsible for accrediting psychology programs and shaping professional standards allows ideology to overshadow scholarship, it risks undermining the credibility of the entire field,” the spokesperson said.

The report, released on Thursday, found that anti-Israel and anti-Jewish activists had “successfully co-opted” the association.

Internal emails showed that association leaders removed references to terrorism from their Oct. 7 statement following objections from an affiliated group.

The report also documented opposition to recognizing a Jewish ethnic psychological association, with critics arguing that Jews benefited from “white privilege.”

“The committee will not only continue to stand up for Jewish psychologists but will work to expose antisemitism wherever it occurs,” the committee spokesperson told JNS.

Following the report’s release, APA president Wendi S. Williams and CEO Arthur C. Evans, Jr., sent an email to colleagues, which JNS has viewed.

“We don’t agree with this report, they wrote. “The American Psychological Association unequivocally condemns antisemitism in all its forms.”

The association said it has “held listening sessions with more than 120 Jewish psychologists and stakeholders to better understand concerns” and “established a Collaborative of Jewish Psychologists to support continued engagement.”

“We recognize that this work requires continued attention and action, and we remain committed to advancing APA’s mission to promote well-being and respect for all,” Williams and Evans wrote.

The Anti-Defamation League issued a public statement on Friday, sent to JNS, thanking the House committee for the report.

“Antisemitism at the American Psychological Association is not isolated,” the organization stated. “It is embedded in its ranks and in its leadership.”

The ADL stated that it and other Jewish organizations “publicly and privately told APA leadership exactly what needed to change, and it failed to act” for more than a year.

“When a healing profession treats one group’s pain with such indifference, Jewish patients are right to wonder whether they will be met with compassion or with contempt,” ADL stated.
news.content: بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. رئیس و مدیر عامل انجمن روانشناسی آمریکا یافته های گزارش مجلس درباره نفرت از یهودیان در انجمن را رد کردند و به همکاران خود در روز پنجشنبه گفتند که APA "جلسات گوش دادن" را با روانشناسان یهودی برگزار کرده است. سخنگوی کمیته آموزش و نیروی کار مجلس به JNS گفت: «اقدامات APA نه تنها یک محیط مضر برای اعضای یهودی ایجاد می‌کند، بلکه نگرانی‌های گسترده‌تری را در مورد این حرفه ایجاد می‌کند.» وقتی سازمانی که مسئول اعتباربخشی برنامه‌های روان‌شناسی و شکل‌دهی استانداردهای حرفه‌ای است اجازه می‌دهد ایدئولوژی بر بورس تحصیلی سایه افکند، خطر تضعیف اعتبار کل حوزه را مطرح می‌کند. این گزارش که روز پنجشنبه منتشر شد، نشان داد که فعالان ضد اسرائیلی و ضدیهودی با "موفقیت آمیز" این انجمن را انتخاب کردند. ایمیل های داخلی نشان داد که رهبران انجمن به دنبال مخالفت های یک گروه وابسته، ارجاع به تروریسم را از بیانیه 7 اکتبر خود حذف کردند. این گزارش همچنین مخالفت با به رسمیت شناختن یک یهودی یهودی را که از "ارتباطات مذهبی نژادی یهودیان انتقاد می کرد" مستند کرد. امتیاز.» سخنگوی کمیته به JNS گفت: «کمیته نه تنها به دفاع از روانشناسان یهودی ادامه خواهد داد، بلکه برای افشای یهودستیزی در هر کجا که رخ دهد، کار خواهد کرد.» پس از انتشار این گزارش، رئیس APA وندی اس. ویلیامز و مدیر عامل اجرایی آن آرتور سی ایوانز جونیور ایمیلی برای همکاران ارسال کردند که JNS با آن موافقت نکرده است.

A witness to the deadly shooting inside a Halloween store at a Bay Area mall described the terrifying scene as shots rang out and she ducked for cover — fearing she was “going to die” as several victims were struck by gunfire.

Jocelyn Lopez Tabares, 15, and her 23-year-old sister were picking up last-minute accessories for their costumes Friday night at the Spirit Halloween store at the Solano Town Center in Fairfield when a barrage of shots erupted.

“I felt like I was going to die,” Lopez Tabares, of Vallejo, told the California Post. “I thought it was going to be my last time living. I didn’t want to die that way.”

The shooting, which left one person dead and six others injured, was a “targeted incident” carried out by a lone gunman, police announced. The suspect remained on the run as of Saturday afternoon. Lopez Tabares, who was standing near the checkout registers, initially mistook the gunfire for popping balloons, until her sister dragged her to the concrete floor, she recalled.

“We were in line getting ready to leave,” Lopez Tabares said. “Out of nowhere, we just hear at least 10 shots go off. I thought it was a balloon popping. I was in shock, and everyone just went down. My sister pulled me down because I couldn’t move. I was so scared.”

As dozens of shoppers scrambled toward the exits in panic, the 15-year-old found herself frozen on the floor.

“All I could hear was people screaming and running from the back to the front,” she said.

The teen then pulled out her cellphone and began recording, determined to document the scene in case she did not survive.

“I just had a feeling to do it… to record for evidence,” she said. “And then after I stopped the video, I called my mom, because what if I wasn’t going to make it out of there?”

The footage shows the panic inside the store as people drop between merchandise racks and frantically take cover. Lopez Tabares said she later shared the clip online after seeing early social media rumors questioning whether a shooting had even happened.

Within minutes of the rapid gunfire, the bustling shop was nearly deserted, leaving only the sisters and a handful of terrified patrons hiding on the floor.

That was when she heard the desperate cries of a frantic mother echoing through the aisles.

“All I could hear was this mom yelling, ‘My baby, he’s dead!’ She was just crying for him,” Lopez Tabares recalled. “She was like, ‘My son… you guys can’t leave him here.’ She looked at my sister, but we couldn’t do anything.”

Authorities have not identified the person who was killed.

Other shoppers inside the retailer described a similarly surreal scene.

Witness Miena Davis told KCRA that shoppers initially froze after hearing popping sounds before a second round of gunfire sent people stampeding toward the mall entrance.

“It was immediate panic,” Davis said. “You heard a mom crying out for their child. And it just was so surreal.”

When Lopez Tabares and her sister finally stood up to run for their lives, they encountered a horrific scene near the exit.

“While we were walking out, there were bodies right there,” she told The Post. “There were two bodies… they were not moving at all.”

Shaken and terrified, the sisters reached their car and drove to their Vallejo home.

The shooting occurred around 8:30 p.m. inside the pop-up retailer at the former Best Buy space.

Fairfield police announced Saturday morning that detectives are investigating the attack as a “targeted incident” carried out by a lone gunman who fled the property before officers arrived.

The FBI’s Sacramento Evidence Response Team has joined local detectives to investigate.

پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. شاهد تیراندازی مرگبار در فروشگاه هالووین در یک مرکز خرید منطقه خلیج، صحنه وحشتناکی را توصیف کرد که صدای شلیک گلوله ها بلند شد و او از ترس این که «بمیرد» به دلیل تیراندازی به چندین قربانی، این صحنه وحشتناک را توصیف کرد. جوسلین لوپز تابارس 15 ساله و خواهر 23 ساله اش جمعه شب در فروشگاه Spirit Halloween در Solano Town Center در فیرفیلد در حال برداشتن لوازم جانبی لحظه آخری برای لباس های خود بودند که رگبار گلوله ها بلند شد. فکر می‌کردم این آخرین باری است که زندگی می‌کنم، نمی‌خواستم اینطور بمیرم.» پلیس اعلام کرد این تیراندازی که منجر به کشته شدن یک نفر و زخمی شدن شش نفر دیگر شد، یک "حادثه هدفمند" بود که توسط یک فرد مسلح انجام شد. مظنون تا بعدازظهر شنبه متواری بود. لوپز تابارس که در نزدیکی صندوق‌های صندوق ایستاده بود، در ابتدا تیراندازی را با بادکنک‌ها اشتباه گرفت تا اینکه خواهرش او را روی زمین سیمانی کشید. لوپز تابارس گفت: «ما در صف آماده رفتن بودیم. "از هیچ جا، ما فقط می شنویم که حداقل 10 گلوله می زند. من فکر می کردم که یک بالون می ترکد. من در شوک بودم و همه پایین آمدند. خواهرم مرا پایین کشید زیرا نمی توانستم حرکت کنم. خیلی ترسیده بودم."
در حالی که ده ها خریدار وحشت زده به سمت در خروجی ها می دویدند، دختر 15 ساله خود را یخ زده روی زمین یافت. «تنها چیزی که می شنیدم این بود که مردم فریاد می زدند و از پشت می دویدند.

news.originalContent:

Americans are getting the majority of their news from social media, according to a new report.

Syracuse University’s Center for the Creator Economy found in its latest monthly Flash Report that social media platforms have overtaken traditional TV news as the most frequently cited source of political and election news among adults surveyed.

The survey of 1,001 adults found that 59% regularly get their news from social media, while 55% turn to those platforms for political information.

Young adults and black Americans were among the groups most likely to rely on social media for news, rather than professional journalists.

Taken together, social platforms and independent outlets — including YouTube, X, TikTok, Instagram, podcasts, Substack and independent newsletters — were cited by 60% of respondents, compared with 32% who cited traditional newsrooms, according to the report.

Leading the pack — YouTube.

The video giant ranks as America’s top individual source for political and election news, capturing 16.5% of readers, narrowly beating broadcast and cable TV news at 16.1% and online news sites at 15.7%.

X registered 14%, Facebook followed with 10.8%, TikTok with 10.4%, Instagram at 7.3%, podcasts at 3.5%, Substack or newsletters at 3.4% and LinkedIn coming in last at a lackluster 0.3%.

The findings also suggest that audiences increasingly judge news by who delivers it, rather than by traditional credentials.

A whopping 61% of Americans reported they trust a well-known independent news creator as much as a well-known professional journalist or a major news organization on political topics. And 67% said who does the reporting matters more than formal journalism credentials.

When it comes to correcting mistakes, 86% said public corrections by independent news creators increase their trust in those creators — the strongest trust-related finding cited in the study.

But traditional journalists haven’t lost all credibility: 79% of respondents still recognized a meaningful difference between independent news creators and professional journalists.

Politics also plays a major role in whom audiences trust.

Republicans generally show greater trust in independent news creators while Democrats lean toward established journalists and news organizations, the report said.

news.originalContent:
The monument has sparked fierce opposition from local governments fearing disruption to traffic and historic views.

The District of Columbia (DC) and the state of Virginia have filed a joint lawsuit to halt the construction of a large triumphal arch sought by United States President Donald Trump.

Filed on Saturday, the lawsuit denounces the project as “flagrantly unlawful” and “legally indefensible”.

It calls on the federal court system to bar construction before it starts.

Otherwise, the lawsuit warns, Trump could claim that pausing construction already under way would pose a national security risk, as he has done with other controversial projects in the past.

“This is not the first time that Defendants have rushed to dramatically remake the District too quickly for courts to intervene,” the lawsuit reads. “This Court should not allow this effort to escape judicial scrutiny.”

Saturday’s complaint brings the total number of lawsuits against the arch to three.

Trump has championed the prospect of building a triumphal arch, similar to the Arc de Triomphe built in Paris during Napoleonic times.

Trump’s arch, however, is designed to stand 30 metres (100 feet) taller than the Statue of Liberty. It would tower from the Memorial Circle in Washington, DC, at 76 metres (250ft).

That colossal scale has prompted outrage, particularly from veterans’ groups who fear the arch would block views of Arlington National Cemetery, a hallowed military grave site.

White House officials maintain that ground could be broken as early as next week, on or around November 5.

On Friday, the administration unveiled a 106-page proposal for the arch to be a 12-storey megastructure, featuring a winged bronze statue of Lady Liberty lifting an eternal flame.

The arch would include two mezzanines and an observation deck with panoramic east-west views, as well as programme spaces, offices and a “fire command centre”.

Trump has previously said the arch would double as a military hub with snipers and drone capabilities.

Construction on the arch would also result in significant traffic changes in the area, including rerouting traffic to nearby roads.

In Saturday’s lawsuit, Attorneys General Brian Schwalb of Washington, DC, and Jay Jones of Virginia pointed to the project’s disruptive footprint as a major concern.

“As soon as defendants break ground on this project, they will inflict irreparable harm on both the District and Virginia,” the lawsuit said.

It warns that the anticipated three-year construction project will stymie commuter traffic, slow down emergency vehicles and generate significant pollution, including “stormwater runoff into the Potomac”.

The lawsuit calls on the court to force the Trump administration to get congressional authorisation before any construction can begin.

The new legal challenge comes on the heels of an October 8 filing by Arlington County, which was the first governmental body to mount a legal action against Trump’s planned monument.

In that lawsuit, the county’s governing board argued that the project would cause “significant harm” to its residents and likely require changes to nearby flight paths.

The first complaint came in February, when a group of Vietnam War veterans and an architectural historian launched an effort to stop the arch.

District Judge Tanya Chutkan is overseeing that case, and she is weighing whether to issue a preliminary injunction to temporarily freeze any construction plans while the court hears arguments.

At a hearing on Friday, Chutkan deferred an immediate ruling but signalled that she would be issuing a decision expeditiously.

She previously ordered the administration to give the court 48 hours’ notice before undertaking any activities related to the construction of the arch.

The monument has already received early approval from the US Commission of Fine Arts, whose members were all tapped by Trump.
news.content:
این بنای تاریخی مخالفت شدید دولت‌های محلی را از ترس ایجاد اختلال در ترافیک و مناظر تاریخی برانگیخته است. منطقه کلمبیا (DC) و ایالت ویرجینیا یک دادخواست مشترک برای توقف ساخت طاق پیروزی بزرگی که دونالد ترامپ رئیس‌جمهور ایالات متحده به دنبال آن بود، تنظیم کرده‌اند. این قانون از سیستم دادگاه فدرال می‌خواهد که ساخت‌وساز را قبل از شروع آن ممنوع کند. در غیر این صورت، دعوای قضایی هشدار می‌دهد که ترامپ می‌تواند ادعا کند که توقف ساخت‌وساز در حال انجام، خطر امنیت ملی را به همراه خواهد داشت، همانطور که او در مورد پروژه‌های بحث‌برانگیز دیگر در گذشته انجام داده است. «این اولین بار نیست که متهمان برای بازسازی چشمگیر منطقه عجله می‌کنند، و دادگاه‌ها خیلی سریع آن را نمی‌خوانند.» این دادگاه نباید اجازه دهد که این تلاش از نظارت قضایی فرار کند.»
شکایت روز شنبه تعداد کل شکایت ها علیه طاق را به سه می رساند. ترامپ از چشم انداز ساخت طاق پیروزی، مشابه طاق پیروزی ساخته شده در پاریس در زمان ناپلئون دفاع کرده است. با این حال، طاق ترامپ به گونه ای طراحی شده است که 30 متر (100 فوت) بلندتر از مجسمه لیبر باشد. این قوس از دایره یادبود در واشنگتن دی سی در ارتفاع 76 متری (250 فوتی) برخاسته است. این مقیاس عظیم خشم را برانگیخته است، به ویژه از سوی گروه های کهنه سربازی که می ترسند طاق نمای قبرستان ملی آرلینگتون، یک مکان مقدس نظامی را مسدود کند. مقامات کاخ سفید متر

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

The doctor who oversaw Christa Pike’s botched execution compared himself to Jesus, still wants her put to death,  and said in his first public comments since the fiasco that he’s willing to finish the job himself.

Dr. Mark Fowler, a 69-year-old grandfather and Bible school teacher studying at seminary, said he believes Pike deserves to die for the brutal 1995 torture and murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, he told New York Magazine.

For two reasons. One, because it would bring “a sense of justice” to her victim’s mother, who was present at the execution attempt.

And two, because he there’s “no doubt” in his mind that the inmates he has personally helped put to death deserved their punishment.

“There are times when you have to draw a line and say, ‘You have traversed socially acceptable norms and we must extract from you the ultimate penalty,” Fowler told the news outlet.

Fowler, whose role during Pike’s execution was to wait in a death chamber anteroom and then pronounce her dead, has taken part in seven executions at $3,000 a job — and believes carrying out the death sentence is a moral obligation.

“How can you morally say, ‘I’m for the death penalty so long as someone else does the work?'” he said. “I do things that nobody wants to do.”

On Sept. 30, Fowler was waiting when prison officials called him into the death chamber where Pike was still breathing after two doses of the lethal drug phenobarbital.

He said he knew something was wrong because it had been 45 minutes since the start of the procedure, which usually takes about 10 minutes.

“She’s not dead,” the warden told him.

Fowler thought it was just a matter of time until she succumbed to the drug. He gave it another half hour.

But at that point, Pike, 50, remained comatose, the deputy commissioner ordered the execution to stop, and Fowler was forced to arrange emergency treatment to save her life.

Investigators later determined that Pike’s IV lines had been improperly placed and caused the drugs to seep into the tissue in her arms instead of entering her bloodstream.

In less than two weeks, she was walking and talking and back in prison at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center in Nashville, Tennessee.

The state’s governor, Bill Lee, suspended executions for the rest of 2026, while Pike’s lawyers try to prevent another lethal injection.

Fowler admitted mistakes were made, saying staff should have responded when Pike complained of arm pain.

“They should have stopped and reassessed, and they didn’t,” he said.

Now he wants Tennessee to consider returning to a three-drug execution cocktail that includes potassium chloride, despite concerns that it’s a painful way to go.

But Fowler doesn’t see himself as a bad guy.

“I’m not an evil, vicious person. I’m not unscrupulous. I’m not uncaring, and I’m not incompetent,” he insisted.

Because of the fever-pitched criticism he’s received over the prison blunder, he’s shut down his Facebook account and accused bullies of trying to make him back down and quit.

“They felt that if they could humiliate me I would step back from it — because I promise you, there ain’t anybody else in Tennessee going to sign up for it now,” he said.

Describing the criticism against him as a “calumny,” he said, “People said bad things about Jesus, didn’t they?”

Pike would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years.

On Oct. 30, in her first statement since the prison catastrophe, she wrote, “I don’t know why I survived that night. I don’t know what comes next … Some days, finding hope is harder than others. For now, I am trying to heal, one day at a time.”

Fowler has a darker take on the matter.

“The Lord gives and the Lord takes away,” he said.
news.content:
پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. دکتری که بر اعدام نادرست کریستا پایک نظارت داشت، خود را با عیسی مقایسه کرد، همچنان خواهان مرگ او است و در اولین نظرات عمومی خود پس از شکست گفت که مایل است این کار را خودش تمام کند. دکتر. مارک فاولر، پدربزرگ 69 ساله و معلم مدرسه انجیل که در حوزه علمیه تحصیل می کند، گفت که او معتقد است که پایک به خاطر شکنجه و قتل وحشیانه 19 ساله کولین اسلمر در سال 1995 سزاوار مرگ است. به دو دلیل. یکی، به این دلیل که «احساس عدالت» را برای مادر قربانیش که در اقدام به اعدام حضور داشت، به ارمغان می آورد. و دو، زیرا او در ذهنش «شکی نیست» که زندانیانی که او شخصاً به اعدام آنها کمک کرده است مستحق مجازات هستند. فاولر به این خبرگزاری گفت: «مواقعی وجود دارد که باید خط و نشان بکشید و بگویید: «شما از هنجارهای قابل قبول اجتماعی عبور کرده‌اید و ما باید مجازات نهایی را از شما بگیریم». فاولر، که نقشش در طول اعدام پایک این بود که در اتاقک مرگ منتظر بماند و سپس اعلام کند که او مرده است، در هفت اعدام با مبلغ 3000 دلار برای هر شغل شرکت کرده است - و معتقد است اجرای حکم اعدام یک تعهد اخلاقی است. او گفت: "چگونه می توانید از نظر اخلاقی بگویید، "من طرفدار مجازات اعدام هستم تا زمانی که شخص دیگری این کار را انجام دهد؟" من کارهایی را انجام می دهم که هیچ کس نمی خواهد انجام دهد.
در سپتامبر در 30 سالگی، فاولر منتظر بود که مقامات زندان او را پس از دو نوبت داروی کشنده فنوباربیتال به اتاق مرگ فراخواندند، جایی که پایک هنوز در حال تنفس بود.

California’s likely next governor is still struggling to say exactly what he’d do about the state’s biggest problems — and a head-scratching answer about the housing crisis is drawing fresh ridicule just before Election Day.

Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra went viral after a recent interview with the San Francisco Chronicle in which reporters pressed him to take a position on one of California’s most contentious housing debates.

The question: Is he a YIMBY or a NIMBY?

Instead of picking a side, Becerra offered a philosophical detour.

“It’s interesting, YIMBY-NIMBY.”

“There’s some people who don’t have a backyard at all, and who never get to engage in that YIMBY-NIMBY debate,” the Democrat added.

The exchange prompted one Chronicle editor to say journalists “tried to get him to say literally anything substantive.”

The terms refer to opposing sides of California’s housing fight. NIMBYs, or “Not In My Backyard” advocates, resist new housing developments in their neighborhoods, while YIMBYs, or “Yes In My Backyard” supporters, push for more construction to address the state’s housing shortage.

Becerra’s answer left plenty of Californians wondering where he actually stands.

Housing advocate Toby Muresianu joked: “Finally, a politician with the courage to say ‘Maybe in my backyard?’ What is a backyard anyway, really?”

Former Los Angeles mayoral candidate Spencer Pratt was less amused.

LMAO Xavier Basura may be the most pathetic NPC candidate I've ever seen. Zero charisma, zero clue, zero campaigning…it's such a slap in the face of CA democrats to run this guy. Almost as if they're pranking them to see how much insanity they'll accept for tribalism. https://t.co/TWZlQegIAJ

“Zero charisma, zero clue, zero campaigning,” Pratt said. “It’s such a slap in the face of CA democrats to run this guy. Almost as if they’re pranking them to see how much insanity they’ll accept for tribalism.”

Others questioned whether Becerra understood the backyard reference was metaphorical, while some tried to decipher whether his answer signaled support for more development or opposition to it.

His campaign website promises an executive order declaring a housing shortage state of emergency and directing state agencies to make housing production a top priority. But he also pledges to “keep communities intact as we build.”

That balancing act has become a recurring feature of Becerra’s campaign.

In August, he told CalMatters that his reluctance to offer detailed policy promises stemmed from a political lesson he learned more than three decades ago.

As a freshman congressman representing the Los Angeles area in 1993, Becerra initially opposed the North American Free Trade Agreement before eventually voting for it after being persuaded that labor protections and a domestic lending program would protect American workers.

He later said those assurances failed to prevent American jobs from being displaced.

“No one gets my vote unless I know what I’m voting for completely,” he told the outlet, describing the experience as a “pivotal lesson.”

Now, Becerra says he doesn’t want to make promises he can’t keep — including putting a number on how many homes he would build as governor.

“I would prefer not to run on inflated promises,” he once said. “I will run on my record.”

But with California voters still grappling with a housing affordability crisis, his reluctance to spell out specifics is giving critics plenty of ammunition.

And Becerra may have little political incentive to change course. Recent polling shows him building a double-digit lead over Republican challenger Steve Hilton in a state where Democrats vastly outnumber Republicans.

بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. فرماندار احتمالی بعدی کالیفرنیا هنوز در تلاش است که دقیقاً در مورد بزرگترین مشکلات این ایالت چه کاری انجام دهد - و پاسخ سرسختانه درباره بحران مسکن درست قبل از روز انتخابات باعث تمسخر تازه می شود. خاویر بسرا، نامزد دموکرات فرمانداری، پس از مصاحبه اخیر با سانفرانسیسکو کرونیکل که در آن خبرنگاران او را تحت فشار قرار دادند تا در یکی از بحث برانگیزترین بحث های مسکن کالیفرنیا موضع بگیرد، به سرعت منتشر شد. این سوال: آیا او یک YIMBY است یا یک NIMBY؟ دموکرات اضافه کرد: «بعضی از مردم هستند که اصلاً حیاط خلوت ندارند و هرگز نمی توانند در بحث YIMBY-NIMBY شرکت کنند.» این تبادل نظر یکی از سردبیران Chronicle را برانگیخت که گفت روزنامه نگاران «سعی کردند او را وادار کنند که به معنای واقعی کلمه هر چیزی را بگوید».
این اصطلاحات به طرف های مخالف جنگ مسکن کالیفرنیا اشاره دارد. طرفداران NIMBY یا «نه در حیاط خلوت من»، در برابر تحولات مسکن جدید در محله‌های خود مقاومت می‌کنند، در حالی که YIMBYها یا حامیان «بله در حیاط خلوت من» برای رفع کمبود مسکن در ایالت به ساخت‌وساز بیشتر فشار می‌آورند. پاسخ بسرا بسیاری از کالیفرنیایی‌ها را متعجب کرد که او واقعاً کجا ایستاده است. شجاعت گفتن "شاید در حیاط خلوت من باشد؟" واقعاً حیاط خلوت چیست؟ اسپنسر پرات، نامزد سابق شهرداری لس آنجلس، کمتر سرگرم شد. news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Nothing demonstrates the moral bankruptcy of national TV than the repeated, two-network appearances of Alex Rodriguez.

Oh, there are challengers. NBC’s hiring of selectively ignorant, self-enriching race-arsonist Al Sharpton is close. So is the networks’ race to hire ready-or-not college coaches moments after they’ve been sacked for the kind of cheating that even head fundraisers posed as college presidents can no longer abide.

But Rodriguez, in addition to being an expensive illusory hire by Fox and for a stretch simultaneously by ESPN — few-to-none intentionally tune in to hear his obligatory pre- and postgame time-killers — is a different kind of stand-alone bad guy.

His impressive MLB batting achievements, generated by illegal drug use, repetitive lies to that fact and defamations of his dead-on accurate accusers, seem to be mere sidebars to the unconscionable creep he is.

Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman insisted Saturday that recent polls showing Gov. Kathy Hochul widening her lead heading into Election Day are “inaccurate,” claiming the race is a “virtual dead heat.”

“Don’t believe those phony polls,” the Nassau County executive told more than 100 supporters at a campaign rally at Juniper Valley Park in Middle Village, Queens.

He was referring to polls released Wednesday by Siena and Marist showing Hochul leading the race by 14 points and 11 points, respectively.

Blakeman also claimed he’ll pull off an upset like former Republican Gov. George Pataki did in 1994, saying polls were “wrong” then as well.

Among those in attendance were Queens GOP Chairman Tony Nunziato, Councilwoman Joann Ariola (R-Queens) and ex-Councilman Robert Holden (D-Queens).

The Nassau County executive was also expected to ramp up his get-out-the-vote efforts later in the day by hitting Halloween parades in Maspeth and Glendale and meeting with voters throughout the Upper East Side, while Hochul was scheduled to make campaign stops in Huntington and Brookhaven on Long Island, and in Brooklyn and Queens.

The campaigns traded Halloween-themed attacks Saturday as they made their final pitches to voters.

Blakeman’s social media accounts posted AI-generated photos and video of Hochul dressed as a witch.

“Forget witches. The real Halloween nightmare is four more years of Kathy Hochul!” Blakeman said on X. “DITCH THE WITCH!”

Hochul’s camp sent out a mass email ripping Blakeman’s armed, civilian-volunteer “emergency special deputy sheriffs” program — labeling it as a “militia clusterf**k.”
news.content:
پوشش بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. بروس بلیکمن، نامزد فرمانداری جمهوری‌خواه، شنبه تاکید کرد که نظرسنجی‌های اخیر که نشان می‌دهد کتی هوچول، فرماندار کاتی هوچول، پیشتاز خود را تا روز انتخابات افزایش می‌دهد، "نادرست" هستند، و ادعا می‌کنند که رقابت "یک گرمای مرده مجازی" است.
مدیر اجرایی کانتی ناسائو در یک گردهمایی مبارزاتی در پارک جونیپر ولی در میدل ویلج، کوئینز به بیش از 100 هوادار گفت: «این نظرسنجی های ساختگی را باور نکنید. اشاره او به نظرسنجی‌هایی بود که روز چهارشنبه توسط سینا و ماریست منتشر شد که نشان می‌داد هوچول به ترتیب با 14 امتیاز و 11 امتیاز در رقابت‌ها پیشتاز است. بلیکمن همچنین ادعا کرد که مانند جورج پاتاکی فرماندار سابق جمهوری‌خواه در سال 1994 ناراحتی ایجاد خواهد کرد و گفت که نظرسنجی‌ها در آن زمان نیز "اشتباه" بوده است. آریولا (R-Queens) و مشاور سابق رابرت هولدن (D-Queens). همچنین انتظار می‌رفت که مدیر کانتی ناسائو تلاش‌های خود را برای رای‌گیری در اواخر روز با انجام رژه‌های هالووین در Maspeth و Glendale و ملاقات با رای‌دهندگان در سراسر Upper East Side افزایش دهد، در حالی که Hochul قرار بود در هانتینگتون و Brookhaven در لانگ‌آیلند توقف کند، و در Brooklyn-Halloween-The Queens آخرین کمپین خود را مورد حمله قرار دادند. برای رای دهندگان حساب‌های رسانه‌های اجتماعی بلیکمن عکس‌ها و ویدیوهای تولید شده توسط هوش مصنوعی را از هوچول در لباس جادوگر منتشر کردند. "جادوگران را فراموش کنید. کابوس واقعی هالووین چهار سال دیگر از کتی هوچول است!" بلیکمن ادامه داد

news.originalContent:
Ranked-choice voting in Alaska could shape key 2026 races, amid a Trump administration lawsuit over two candidates named Dan Sullivan.

In Alaska, a controversy is unfolding over whether two Senate candidates with roughly the same name will cancel each other out.

The debate has shone a spotlight on a relatively uncommon style of voting in the United States: a system known as “ranked choice”.

Only two states in the United States — Alaska and Maine — employ ranked-choice voting throughout their territory, though major cities like New York have also embraced the practice.

Ranked-choice ballots allow voters to rank candidates in order of preference, rather than choosing just one. If a voter’s first choice does not win a majority, their vote can be transferred to their second pick.

With US midterm elections set for November 3, ranked-choice voting could play a role in closely watched races, including the Alaska Senate battle.

Here’s a guide on how ranked-choice voting works in the US:

Proponents of ranked-choice voting believe the practice frees voters from the pressure of having to vote pragmatically. They no longer have to cast their ballot based on the candidate most likely to win.

Instead, supporters say that ranked-choice voting allows people to support the candidate they prefer the most, without the fear of “wasting” their vote should that candidate prove to be unpopular.

Advocates for ranked-choice voting also argue that the system reduces the spoiler effect, whereby a third-party or lesser-known candidate draws votes from a similar major-party candidate.

They also frame the system as a boon for democracy, by encouraging more diverse viewpoints to compete in elections and offering an incentive for candidates to work together.

Critics argue that ranked-choice ballots make voting and vote-counting more complicated.

They also fear it could slow down the tallying of election results, undermining confidence in the outcome.

A 2025 study published in the journal Political Behavior cited data suggesting that 4.8 percent of ranked-choice ballots are “improperly marked” — though it clarified that not all of those ballots are invalidated as a result.

On a ranked-choice ballot, voters get to number their candidates in order of preference. If their first choice doesn’t win, their vote automatically counts for their next choice instead.

If one candidate receives more than 50 percent of first-choice votes, that candidate wins.

If no candidate secures a majority, the candidate with the fewest votes is eliminated. Ballots for that candidate are redistributed to voters’ next-ranked choices, and the votes are tallied again.

This continues until a candidate wins a majority of votes still counted in the final round.

If a voter ranks only one candidate and that candidate is eliminated, their ballot cannot transfer to another candidate.

Unlike a traditional runoff election, which requires voters to return to the polls, ranked-choice voting can determine a winner through successive rounds of counting in a single election.

Maine adopted ranked-choice voting in 2016 after concerns emerged about candidates winning elections without majority support. It first used the system in congressional elections in 2018.

Alaska voters approved the system through a 2020 ballot initiative. The state uses open primaries in which all candidates compete, with the top four advancing to a general election decided by ranked-choice voting.

Alaska’s ranked-choice voting system could come under scrutiny in this year’s Senate race, where two candidates named Dan Sullivan appear on the ballot.

The potential for voter confusion raises questions about whether some voters could accidentally rank the wrong candidate, potentially affecting how votes are distributed in successive rounds of ballot-counting.

State officials have taken steps to differentiate the two Sullivans on the ballot.

The incumbent, Senator Dan S Sullivan, is listed as a registered Republican and the incumbent, while his challenger, retired teacher Daniel J Sullivan Jr, has no party identification next to his name.

Still, the teacher’s inclusion has been the source of ongoing controversy, particularly in the wake of a New York Times report signalling he may have been recruited by Democrats as a spoiler candidate.

Republicans have raised concerns that having two Sullivans on the ballot could confuse voters and draw support away from the senator.

The teacher, meanwhile, has said his candidacy is genuine. In June, the Alaska Supreme Court allowed the vote to proceed with the participation of both Sullivans.

But the controversy has prompted US President Donald Trump to sue Alaska, seeking to block certification of the Senate election results if the incumbent Dan S Sullivan loses.

The lawsuit argues that confusion over the two candidates’ names could affect the outcome, but Alaska officials and Democrats are challenging the case.

Under the US Constitution, election administration falls to the states, and the lawsuit has raised concerns that the federal government might seek to meddle in Alaska’s vote count.

Ranked-choice voting is used in various local elections nationwide, including in New York City and San Francisco. Hawaii also uses it for certain special elections, while Washington, DC, adopted it for federal and local elections beginning in 2026.

Earlier this year, Virginia approved legislation expanding the use of ranked-choice voting.

But the system remains contested by some states. An estimated 19 states have laws prohibiting or restricting ranked-choice voting, according to the National Conference of State Legislatures.
news.content:
در بحبوحه شکایت دولت ترامپ بر سر دو نامزد به نام دن سالیوان، رای گیری انتخابی در آلاسکا می تواند رقابت های کلیدی سال 2026 را شکل دهد. در آلاسکا، بحث بر سر اینکه آیا دو نامزد سنا با نام تقریباً یکسان یکدیگر را لغو خواهند کرد یا خیر، در جریان است. تنها دو ایالت در ایالات متحده - آلاسکا و مین - در سراسر قلمرو خود از رای گیری با انتخاب رتبه بندی استفاده می کنند، اگرچه شهرهای بزرگی مانند نیویورک نیز این عمل را پذیرفته اند. برگه های رای رتبه بندی شده به رای دهندگان این امکان را می دهد که کاندیداها را به جای انتخاب فقط یکی، به ترتیب اولویت رتبه بندی کنند. اگر انتخاب اول یک رای دهنده اکثریت را به دست نیاورد، رای او می تواند به انتخاب دوم منتقل شود. از آنجایی که انتخابات میان دوره ای ایالات متحده برای 3 نوامبر تعیین شده است، رای گیری با انتخاب رتبه بندی می تواند نقشی در رقابت هایی که از نزدیک تماشا می شوند، از جمله نبرد سنای آلاسکا ایفا کند. در اینجا راهنمای نحوه عملکرد رای گیری با انتخاب رتبه بندی در ایالات متحده آمده است:
طرفداران رای گیری با انتخاب رتبه بندی بر این باورند که این رویه رای دهندگان را از فشار رای دادن عملی رها می کند. آنها دیگر مجبور نیستند رای خود را بر اساس نامزدی که به احتمال زیاد برنده می شود، به صندوق بیندازند. درعوض، حامیان می‌گویند که رای‌گیری با انتخاب رتبه‌بندی به مردم اجازه می‌دهد تا از نامزدی که بیشتر از همه ترجیح می‌دهند، بدون ترس از «هدر رفتن» رأی‌شان حمایت کنند، در صورتی که آن نامزد محبوبیت نداشته باشد. مدافعان رأی‌دهی رتبه‌بندی شده همچنین استدلال می‌کنند که این سیستم اثر اسپویلر را کاهش می‌دهد.

news.originalContent:
Turkish president hosts Zelenskyy in Istanbul as the two leaders agree to work on a new Black Sea grain corridor.

Turkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has urged both Russia and Ukraine to stop targeting civilian ships in the Black Sea, as he and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy agreed to work on a new grain corridor through the waterway.

Erdogan made the comments on Saturday at a joint news conference with Zelenskyy in Istanbul, saying attacks on civilian vessels were unacceptable, whoever carries them out.

The talks came on the same day US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was growing international interest in a limited ceasefire in the Black Sea to secure grain and energy shipments by both countries.

“It is clear that attacks against civilian vessels and actions that further escalate tensions in the Black Sea serve no one’s interests,” Erdogan said.

“We cannot accept these attacks under any circumstances, regardless of who carries them out or what justification is offered,” he said, adding, “We call on all parties to act responsibly on this matter.”

Turkiye, which maintains ties with both Moscow and Kyiv, has been angered by the strikes on commercial shipping.

Ankara has sent Russia and Ukraine a proposal to end attacks, but says neither side has acted on it.

Zelenskyy accused Russia of making the situation in the Black Sea difficult and said a significant part of his conversation with Erdogan focused on security there.

“Today, I reached an agreement with President Erdogan to work on the Black Sea grain corridor,” he said.

He said Turkiye supports efforts to ensure safe navigation in the Black Sea and restore normal living conditions.

“We discussed with President Erdogan some ideas and proposals that can help,” Zelenskyy said, thanking the Turkish leader for the dialogue.

Erdogan said talks to restore safe navigation would continue.

“I believe that reaching an agreement on this issue would also give fresh impetus to efforts to secure lasting peace in Ukraine,” he said.

The US is reviewing proposals by Turkiye and India to get grain shipments moving, according to Rubio.

“This is threatening the world for food security and some energy security as well,” Rubio told a news conference in Atlanta, Georgia, following a G20 foreign ministers meeting. “We’d like to achieve it. It doesn’t solve the war, but at least it solves a unique aspect of it.”

Erdogan also welcomed renewed momentum behind efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war through diplomatic means, pointing in particular to US President Donald Trump’s initiative.

“At this point, we maintain that there can be no losers in a just peace,” he said, adding, “I would like to emphasise that we stand ready to make every possible effort to pave the way for peace”.

Turkiye has hosted several rounds of talks between Russia and Ukraine aimed at a lasting ceasefire and peace deal, which Erdogan said showed that “tangible results can be achieved through diplomacy”.

In a phone call with Trump on Wednesday, Erdogan said Turkiye was ready to support efforts to revive the diplomatic process and end the war, according to the Turkish president’s office.

Last week, the Kremlin said the next round of talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US was planned to resume in November in the United Arab Emirates.

Zelenskyy said he had discussed that format with Erdogan, along with other options, including involving Turkiye, Europe and other partners, as well as the possibility of a meeting in Turkiye.

“Strong decisions are needed for there to be peace,” he said. “And it is necessary at all levels to send signals to Russia that there is no alternative to peace and that support for Ukraine will continue.”
news.content: رئیس جمهور ترکیه میزبان زلنسکی در استانبول بود زیرا دو رهبر برای کار بر روی یک کریدور جدید غلات دریای سیاه به توافق رسیدند. رجب طیب اردوغان، رئیس جمهور ترکیه از روسیه و اوکراین خواسته است که هدف قرار دادن کشتی های غیرنظامی در دریای سیاه را متوقف کنند، زیرا او و رئیس جمهور اوکراین ولودیمیر زلنسکی توافق کردند روی یک کریدور غلات جدید از طریق آبراه کار کنند. اردوغان این اظهارات را روز شنبه در یک کنفرانس خبری مشترک با زلنسکی در استانبول بیان کرد و گفت که حملات به کشتی‌های غیرنظامی غیرقابل قبول است، هر کسی که این حملات را انجام دهد. این مذاکرات در همان روزی انجام شد که مارکو روبیو، وزیر امور خارجه آمریکا، گفت که علاقه بین‌المللی به آتش‌بس محدود در دریای سیاه برای تامین امنیت محموله‌های غلات و انرژی توسط هر دو کشور افزایش یافته است. اردوغان گفت: واضح است که حملات علیه کشتی‌های غیرنظامی و اقداماتی که باعث تشدید تنش‌ها در دریای سیاه می‌شود، به نفع هیچ‌کس نیست. ترکیه که با مسکو و کیف روابط خود را حفظ می کند، از حملات به کشتی های تجاری خشمگین شده است. آنکارا پیشنهادی برای پایان دادن به حملات به روسیه و اوکراین ارسال کرده است، اما می گوید هیچ یک از طرفین به آن عمل نکرده است. زلنسکی روسیه را به سخت کردن اوضاع در دریای سیاه متهم کرد و گفت: بخش مهمی از گفتگوی خود با اردوغان بر امنیت آنجا متمرکز بود. «امروز به توافق رسیدم.

Hackers have targeted Binance, the world’s largest exchange.

It is being called the biggest cryptocurrency heist in history – and the shocks are still reverberating through the industry.

The target of this recent hack was Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange.

Attackers stole about $6.3bn in client assets.

Analysts suspect hackers backed by the North Korean government carried out the theft.

Critics are calling for more regulations to restore the trust of investors.

So, is cryptocurrency still safe? And can these kinds of attacks even be prevented?

Presenter: Mohammed Jamjoom

Lee Reiners – Lecturing fellow at Duke University and a former US Federal Reserve Bank examiner

Geoff White – Investigative journalist and author of The Lazarus Heist

Anupam Chander – Professor of law and technology at Georgetown University, who specialises in the global regulation of new technologies

news.originalContent:
دبیر شورای عالی امنیت ملی ایران، گفته است که برای تغییر دکترین هسته‌ای تصمیم جدیدی گرفته‌ نشده است اما ادامه داده که ملت ایران «دارای مطالباتی است.»

سرلشکر محسن رضایی، به تلویزیون ایران گفته است «هنوز در دولت، در حکومت تصمیم جدیدی گرفته نشده. البته این بحث الان مطرح است که اگر دوباره جنگ بشود، آیا ما می‌خواهیم همان دکترین سابق را داشته باشیم یا نداشته باشیم ولی هیچ تصمیم جدیدی به صورت رسمی و حکومتی گرفته نشده است.»

در ادبیات سیاسی و موضوعات مرتبط با اشاعه تسلیحات هسته‌ای، بازنگری در دکترین هسته‌ای عموما به معنای تغییر سیاست با هدف دستیابی به سلاح اتمی است.

آقای رضایی در اظهارات تازه خود گفته است «ملت ایران دارای مطالباتی است. دنبال یک منطقی هستند. بالاخره آنها می‌بینند دشمن آمده تمام مراکز هسته‌ای ما رو زده است. خب به چه دلیل زده؟ ما که به تمام بازرسی‌های آژانس ما پاسخ مثبت دادیم. در تمام سایت‌های ما دوربین داشتند. وقتی مردم اینها را می‌بینند قاعدتاً خواسته‌شان از ما این است که برای چه می‌خواهید  این وضع را ادامه بدهید.»

یک روز پیش از این محمدجواد حاج‌علی‌اکبری، امام جمعه موقت تهران، در خطبه های نماز جمعه خواستار بازنگری در دکترین هسته‌ای جمهوری اسلامی ایران شده بود.

او گفته بود «این موضوع واکنشی شتاب‌زده و هیجانی نیست، بلکه برآمده از آگاهی و تجربه تاریخی ملت ایران در مواجهه با بدعهدی‌های آمریکاست و ریشه در حق ملت برای برخورداری از امنیت و زندگی عزتمندانه دارد.»ش منتشر نشده است.

ایران تاکنون هدف از برنامه اتمی خود را صلح آمیز اعلام کرده است اما کشورهای غربی و آژانس بین‌المللی انرژی اتمی خواهان شفافیت درباره آن هستند.

آقای رضایی در اظهارات تازه خود گفته است که رافائل گروسی، مدیرکل آژانس «مزدور رژیم صهیونی است و همه مسائل ما از زمان او آغاز شد.»

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

دوره مدیرکلی آقای گروسی با پس خروج آمریکا از توافق اتمی برجام همزمان بوده که آغاز یک دوره پر تنش بین ایران و قدرت‌های غربی بوده است.

در این دوره ایران در واکنش به بازگشت تحریم‌های آمریکا سطوح غنی‌سازی خود را بالا برد، ذخایراورانیومش را افزایش داد و اجرای توافق برای نظارت های گسترده آژانس را به مرور کاهش داد.

این موضوع به بحران اتمی این کشور دامن زده است. از جمله دولت‌های غربی از جمله می‌گویند درباره غنی‌سازی اورانیوم در ایران با سطوح بالا که کاربرد دوگانه از جمله در سلاح اتمی دارد، نگرانی‌هایی دارند و آژانس اعلام کرده که قادر نیست پس از حملات سال گذشته اسرائیل و آمریکا به تاسیسات اتمی ایران، نظارت کاملی بر همه جنبه‌های برنامه اتمی این کشور داشته باشد.

پیش از جنگ  اخیر برخی از مقام های ایرانی همچون کمال خرازی، رئیس شورای راهبردی روابط خارجی ایران که در حمله اسرائیل کشته شد، و محمد اسلامی، رئیس سازمان انرژی اتمی ایران، از توانایی این کشور برای ساخت سلاح اتمی سخن گفته بودند، اما تأکید داشتند که با وجود این توانایی، جمهوری اسلامی ایران با استناد به نظر علی خامنه‌ای، قصدی برای ساخت آن ندارد.

رهبر پیشین جمهوری اسلامی دو دهه پیش در یک سخنرانی گفته بود که تولید، نگهداری و استفاده از سلاح اتمی را حرام می‌داند.

مقام‌های دولتی پس از این اظهارات، آن را با عنوان «فتوای اتمی» به‌عنوان سند به سازمان ملل متحد ارائه کردند و هر بار که پرونده اتمی ایران وضعیت بحرانی‌تری پیدا می‌کرد، با استناد به آن اعلام می‌کردند که جمهوری اسلامی از ساخت هرگونه سلاح اتمی خودداری خواهد کرد و از نظر مذهبی نیز آن را حرام می‌داند.

مجتبی خامنه‌ای که پس از کشته‌شدن پدرش به جانشینی او انتخاب شد، تاکنون موضع صریحی در این باره نگرفته است.

او تاکنون در انظار عمومی ظاهر نشده و فیلم یا فایل صوتی از او پس از رسیدن به جانشینی پدرش منتشر نشده است.

در این دوره ایران در واکنش به بازگشت تحریم‌های آمریکا سطوح غنی‌سازی خود را بالا برد، ذخایراورانیومش را افزایش داد و اجرای توافق برای نظارت های گسترده آژانس را به مرور کاهش داد.

این موضوع به بحران اتمی این کشور دامن زده است. از جمله دولت‌های غربی از جمله می‌گویند درباره غنی‌سازی اورانیوم در ایران با سطوح بالا که کاربرد دوگانه از جمله در سلاح اتمی دارد، نگرانی‌هایی دارند و آژانس اعلام کرده که قادر نیست پس از حملات سال گذشته اسرائیل و آمریکا به تاسیسات اتمی ایران، نظارت کاملی بر همه جنبه‌های برنامه اتمی این کشور داشته باشد.

پیش از جنگ  اخیر برخی از مقام های ایرانی همچون کمال خرازی، رئیس شورای راهبردی روابط خارجی ایران که در حمله اسرائیل کشته شد، و محمد اسلامی، رئیس سازمان انرژی اتمی ایران، از توانایی این کشور برای ساخت سلاح اتمی سخن گفته بودند، اما تأکید داشتند که با وجود این توانایی، جمهوری اسلامی ایران با استناد به نظر علی خامنه‌ای، قصدی برای ساخت آن ندارد.

رهبر پیشین جمهوری اسلامی دو دهه پیش در یک سخنرانی گفته بود که تولید، نگهداری و استفاده از سلاح اتمی را حرام می‌داند.

مقام‌های دولتی پس از این اظهارات، آن را با عنوان «فتوای اتمی» به‌عنوان سند به سازمان ملل متحد ارائه کردند و هر بار که پرونده اتمی ایران وضعیت بحرانی‌تری پیدا می‌کرد، با استناد به آن اعلام می‌کردند که جمهوری اسلامی از ساخت هرگونه سلاح اتمی خودداری خواهد کرد و از نظر مذهبی نیز آن را حرام می‌داند.

مجتبی خامنه‌ای که پس از کشته‌شدن پدرش به جانشینی او انتخاب شد، تاکنون موضع صریحی در این باره نگرفته است.

او تاکنون در انظار عمومی ظاهر نشده و فیلم یا فایل صوتی از او پس از رسیدن به جانشینی پدرش منتشر نشده است.

news.originalContent:
A calm head on young shoulders, Arafat Minhas has swiftly earned the reputation of a match-winner for Pakistan.

At five wickets down with 125 required off 79 balls, Pakistan were teetering on the edge of yet another batting collapse when Arafat Minhas walked in to bat in the  final of the One-Day International (ODI) tri-nation cricket series against Sri Lanka.

An expectant home crowd in Lahore was on tenterhooks as the 21-year-old all-rounder began his batting partnership with Hasan Nawaz under the floodlights of the Gaddafi Stadium on Saturday.

Minhas, who had gone wicketless in Sri Lanka’s innings, showed few signs of the pressure mounting on the young batting pair and began the repair job.

Within a few overs, the run chase swayed back in Pakistan’s favour but the final remained tense.

With the hosts needing 39 runs from 27 balls, Sri Lanka’s Dasun Shanaka bowled a delivery at length, angling the ball into Minhas.

Unnerved by the occasion and his own lack of experience, the batter swung his bat across the line and sent the ball soaring over midwicket for six to ignite the crowd and rekindle lost hope.

Following this defining moment of his innings, Arafat coolly went on to hit four more sixes, finish with 61 runs off 31 balls, help Pakistan clinch the trophy and bag himself the player of the series award.

He ended the series with nine wickets and 149 runs, including two half-centuries.

Commentators on the host broadcast ran out of superlatives for the promising all-rounder, who admitted that he “enjoyed the pressure” of the final run-chase and tried to remain calm.

“The team needed someone to believe that we could achieve the target.”

Before shining with the bat in the final, Arafat produced one of the finest bowling performances of his fledgling international career against England in Rawalpindi on October 10.

After scoring 59 off 58 balls to help Pakistan recover from 81-4 and post 302-9, Minhas took six wickets for 40 runs as England were bowled out for 215, handing Pakistan an 87-run win.

England were at 91 without losing a wicket before Arafat dismantled their batting order.

Among his victims was swashbuckling batter Harry Brook, who was bowled for five by a delivery that turned past his attempted defensive shot and hit the stumps.

The England captain was left stunned at the crease and in the post-match media talk.

“Is he under 21? I didn’t know,” Brook said after the match.

More plaudits poured in as Minhas showed his all-round skills on the field.

“A half-century, six wickets and a run out. Mike Hesson wants all-round cricketers and he’s found one in Arafat Minhas,” former England captain Nasser Hussain said during the broadcast.

The performance made him the third Pakistani to score a half-century and take at least five wickets in a men’s ODI after Shahid Afridi and Abdul Razzaq.

On his ODI debut against Australia in May, Arafat took 5-32, becoming the first Pakistani to claim a five-wicket haul on debut, as well as winning the player of the series award.

“I prefer not to label players as batting or bowling all-rounders,” Minhas later said in an interview with the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB). “I’d rather be seen as a complete all-rounder.”

Thirteen years earlier, Minhas dreamed of becoming a fast bowler like every other aspiring Pakistani cricketer.

But the then-eight-year-old was handed a leather cricket ball and instructed to take up left-arm spin by his father, Kashif, who spent years helping Arafat develop the all-round skills that are now helping Pakistan win matches.

Kashif had represented his hometown team, Multan, in under-19 cricket but was forced to give up on his dream – “with a heavy heart” – by his father, who urged him to take over the family’s car showroom business.

Years later, watching his sons play with toy eggs and plastic balls, Kashif saw a spark.

“When I observed them, I saw their playing style wasn’t ordinary; it seemed like a natural gift and a blessing from God,” Kashif told Al Jazeera. “I thought: ‘why not train them for professional cricket’?”

He would go on to buy full kits for his sons, setting them on the path towards professional cricket.

“My father handed me a hard ball when I was about eight or nine and I’ve bowled left-arm spin ever since [but] In tape-ball cricket, I used to bowl fast,” Minhas explained when asked about his control on his bowling variations.

Minhas rapidly progressed through Pakistan’s age-group system, becoming the country’s best under-16 player in his final year before breaking into the under-19 team.

In 2020, when the COVID-19 pandemic lockdown threatened to interrupt his sons’ development, Kashif built a cricket practice facility on the rooftop of his house in Multan.

A net, a mat pitch and floodlights were installed to ensure that “practice wouldn’t stop”.

In 2024, when Pakistan reached the semifinals of the ICC Under-19 World Cup and lost to Australia by one wicket, Minhas played a key role in the team’s progress in the tournament.

Given his standout performances, the young all-rounder’s elevation to the senior team seemed inevitable.

Minhas’s younger brother, Sameer, is a prodigious right-handed opening batter who has also made significant progress.

Last week, he was included in Pakistan’s Test squad for the two-match series against Sri Lanka in November.

Playing his first season of first-class cricket, Sameer scored 405 runs in seven matches, following his own promising spell with Pakistan’s under-19 team. Their youngest brother, Abdullah, is also pursuing cricket as a left-handed batter and leg-spinner.

“To move forward, I’ll improve and put in whatever extra work is required,” Minhas said after the England match. “This isn’t the final goal. The ultimate goal is much further ahead.”

Kashif’s ambition extends beyond one son’s career. He wishes for all three boys to play together for Pakistan and win an international trophy – a dream that would give a new ending to the cricketing journey he had to abandon.

“My ultimate dream is to see all three of my sons play together in the Pakistan playing XI and bring home an ICC trophy for Pakistan. That’s the day my dream will be complete, and that void will truly be filled.”

news.originalContent:
Demonstrations in London and Edinburgh come days before a UK Supreme Court appeal challenging the group’s proscription.

Police have arrested at least 139 people after protesters defied a warning not to attend a rally in London against the proscription of Palestine Action, which is classified as a “terrorist” organisation under United Kingdom law.

Hundreds of people gathered outside the United States embassy on Saturday to oppose the ban, which came into effect in July last year under the government of then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

The demonstration comes ahead of a Supreme Court appeal on Wednesday challenging the campaign group’s proscription.

In a post on X on Saturday evening, London’s Metropolitan Police said “139 people have now been arrested”, up from the 48 it said it detained earlier in the day. “The majority of arrests have been for expressing support for a proscribed organisation,” it said.

Responding to the police statement, Labour Party MP John McDonnell posted on X, saying someone protesting against the government’s decision to proscribe an organisation cannot be “automatically interpreted” as them supporting that organisation and “therefore committing an arrestable offence”.

He added that he believes the government “made the wrong decision in proscribing Palestine Action as a terrorist organisation”.

Saturday’s rally is the first mass protest against the proscription since Prime Minister Andy Burnham assumed office in July.

The decision to designate the group a “terrorist” organisation has triggered uproar among sections of British society, with critics arguing that it is part of a wider crackdown aimed at silencing pro-Palestine voices. The proscription means Palestine Action has been added to a list of banned organisations that also includes al-Qaeda and ISIL (ISIS).

Protesters also gathered outside the US consulate in Edinburgh, the Scottish capital. There have been no reports of arrests there.

Demonstrators in both London and Edinburgh could be seen holding placards reading “I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action”.

Defend Our Juries, which organised the protests, said Saturday’s arrests took the total number of people detained for defying the Palestine Action ban to more than 4,000 since July 2025.

“It is truly dystopian that there have now been over 4,000 arrests under terror laws for peaceful vigils silently expressing opposition to genocide and support for the protest group Palestine Action,” a spokesperson for the group said, as reported by UK news agency Press Association.

“The ban on Palestine Action was straight out of [US President Donald] Trump’s playbook, so it’s fitting that this significant milestone has been reached on Halloween and outside the US embassy,” the spokesperson added, saying the proscription was about the UK government “appeasing Trump and the Israeli weapons companies that Palestine Action disrupted, not about any kind of terrorist threat”.

Felix Jakens, Amnesty International UK’s head of communications and campaigns, also called on the government to reverse Palestine Action’s proscription.

“The sight yet again of grandparents, teenagers and everyone in between being hauled into police vans for peacefully holding placards is a disgraceful attack on freedom of speech,” Jakens said in response to the arrests on Saturday.

“It’s past time for the government to drop the proscription of Palestine Action and reform our laws so that communities have more power to demonstrate on the issues they care about, not less.”
news.content: تظاهرات در لندن و ادینبورگ چند روز قبل از درخواست تجدیدنظر دادگاه عالی بریتانیا در به چالش کشیدن ممنوعیت این گروه برگزار می شود. پلیس حداقل 139 نفر را پس از اینکه معترضان از هشدار برای شرکت نکردن در تجمع لندن علیه ممنوعیت اقدام فلسطین که طبق قوانین بریتانیا به عنوان یک سازمان "تروریستی" طبقه بندی می شود سرپیچی کردند، دستگیر کرد. صدها نفر روز شنبه در مقابل سفارت ایالات متحده تجمع کردند تا با ممنوعیتی که در ژوئیه سال گذشته در دولت نخست وزیر وقت کیر استارمر اجرایی شد، مخالفت کنند. این تظاهرات پیش از درخواست تجدیدنظر در دادگاه عالی در روز چهارشنبه برگزار می شود که ممنوعیت گروه کمپین را به چالش می کشد. پلیس متروپولیتن لندن در پستی در روز شنبه عصر در ایکس گفت: «در حال حاضر 139 نفر دستگیر شده اند، از 48 نفری که در اوایل روز بازداشت شده بود. در این بیانیه آمده است: «بیشتر دستگیری ها به دلیل ابراز حمایت از یک سازمان ممنوع بوده است. در پاسخ به بیانیه پلیس، جان مک دانل، نماینده حزب کارگر در ایکس پست کرد و گفت که کسی که به تصمیم دولت برای ممنوع کردن یک سازمان معترض است، نمی‌تواند «به طور خودکار» به عنوان حمایت از آن سازمان و «بنابراین مرتکب یک جرم قابل دستگیری» تفسیر شود. تظاهرات روز شنبه اولین تظاهرات گسترده علیه ممنوعیت ممنوعیت از زمان روی کار آمدن اندی برنهام نخست وزیر در ماه ژوئیه است. تصمیم برای تعیین
